title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Biology (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Biology (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A review article is written by reading
options: original articles on the same topic
analyzing primary data or secondary data
questions.explanation: A review article synthesizes information from original articles on the same topic.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is not true about fungi?
options: They reproduce either asexual or sexual or both
They were evolved before the evolution of bacteria
questions.explanation: Fungi evolved after bacteria, making the statement incorrect.

questions.questionText: During osmosis the movement of solvent molecules takes place from solution whose osmotic pressure is lower?
questions.explanation: Osmosis occurs from a hypotonic solution to a hypertonic solution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is not correct about photosynthesis?
options: Red, blue and violet wavelengths of visible light are least absorbed
questions.explanation: Red, blue, and violet wavelengths are actually absorbed, making this statement incorrect.

questions.questionText: The consumers that eat only plants can be called as
questions.explanation: Herbivores are defined as consumers that eat only plants.

questions.questionText: Which of the following cellular structures are common to prokaryotes and eukaryotes?
options: Ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi bodies
questions.explanation: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, and ribosomes are found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

questions.questionText: If a student concluded a newly discovered mammal Q feeds its young on milk based on the fact that 'Mammals feed their young on milk'. This is an example of
questions.explanation: This is an example of deductive reasoning.

questions.questionText: During photosynthesis, where did the O2 come from?
questions.explanation: O2 is produced from the splitting of water (H2O) during photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: Two solutions are separated by a partially permeable membrane. Solutions 1 has 1g/mL, while solution 2 has 2g/mL concentration of glucose. Which of the following best describes what will happen to the amount of glucose, volume of water and concentration of solution?
options: The concentration of glucose will increase in solution 1 as the volume of water decreases, while the concentration of glucose will decrease in solution 2 as the volume of water increases.
The concentration of glucose will increase in solution 1 as the amount of glucose increases, while the concentration of glucose will decrease in solution 2 as the amount of glucose decreases.

The concentration of glucose in solution 1 will decrease as the volume of water increases in solution 1, while the concentration of glucose will increase in solution 2 as the volume of water decreases.
The volume of water increases in solution 1 as the amount of glucose decreases, while the volume of water will decrease in solution 2 as the amount of glucose increases.
questions.explanation: In osmosis, water moves from a region of lower solute concentration (solution 1, 1g/mL) to a region of higher solute concentration (solution 2, 2g/mL) across a semipermeable membrane. As water moves out of solution 1, its volume decreases while the glucose concentration increases (same amount of glucose in less water). Conversely, as water moves into solution 2, its volume increases while the glucose concentration decreases (same amount of glucose in more water).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct comparison of mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis produces four daughter cells, while meiosis produces two daughter cells.
Mitosis produces genetically identical cells, while meiosis produces cloned cells.
The daughter cells produced by mitosis are diploid, but those produced by meiosis are haploid.
Two cell divisions occur in mitosis, but in four cell divisions occur meiosis.
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces diploid cells, while meiosis produces haploid cells.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not the characteristics of Basidiomycetes?
options: They have fruiting structure known as basidiocap or basidioma
They have a sexual spore known as basidiospore
They produce clamp connection in certain types of hyphae
questions.explanation: Basidiomycetes typically have septate hyphae, not coenocytic.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a harmful insect?
questions.explanation: House flies are harmful insects as they can transmit various diseases to humans by carrying pathogens. Lac insects are actually beneficial as they produce lac, a resinous secretion used in various products. Honey bees and silk-worms are also beneficial insects.

questions.questionText: The anterior and posterior body region of insects are called ______________ and ______________, respectively.
questions.explanation: In insects, the anterior region is the head and the posterior region is the abdomen, with the thorax in between.

questions.questionText: Why is mitochondria said to be the powerhouse of the cell?
options: It is a site for carbohydrates production
It is a site of respiration to generate energy
It is a site where carbohydrates break down to provide ATP
It is a site for carbohydrates storage in the form of starch
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are known for their role in energy production through respiration.

questions.questionText: Largest protozoal parasite is
questions.explanation: Balantidium coli is the largest protozoal parasite.

questions.questionText: The hard outer body covering of insect is called ______________.
questions.explanation: The exoskeleton is the hard outer covering of insects.

questions.questionText: One is not a marsupial.
questions.explanation: Manatee is not a marsupial; it is an aquatic mammal belonging to the order Sirenia. Opossums, kangaroos, and bandicoots are all marsupials characterized by giving birth to undeveloped young that continue to develop in a pouch.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Aquaculture pond must be drained per year in order to collect fish from pond
Overgrowth of algae in aquafarm can cause high oxygen shortage for fish respiration in aquafarm
Herbicide is most eco-friendly to remove aquatic plants in aquaculture pond
Decomposition of algae in aquafarm increases the concentration of oxygen in water
questions.explanation: Overgrowth of algae can lead to oxygen depletion in aquaculture ponds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following two sentences correctly describe anaerobic respiration in mammalian cells and yeast cells?
options: Anaerobic respiration in mammalian cells occurs only in the absence of oxygen. Yeast cells also undergo anaerobic respiration, which produces carbon dioxide bubbles that cause bread dough to rise.
In anaerobic respiration in mammalian cells, more ATP per glucose are made compared to aerobic respiration. Wine, beer, and other alcohols including biofuels use anaerobic respiration of yeast cells.
In anaerobic respiration in mammalian cells, buildup of carbon dioxide causes muscle fatigue and cramps. Anaerobic respiration in yeast cell does not produce ATP molecule.
In anaerobic respiration in mammalian cell, more ATP is produced than in aerobic respiration. In anaerobic respiration in yeast cell, lactate is produced and collected as biofuel.
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in mammalian cells (also called lactic acid fermentation) occurs when oxygen is limited or absent, producing lactic acid as an end product. In yeast cells, anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation) produces ethanol and carbon dioxide as end products. The CO2 bubbles are what cause bread dough to rise during baking. The other statements contain inaccuracies: anaerobic respiration produces less ATP than aerobic respiration, not more; muscle fatigue is caused by lactic acid buildup, not CO2; and yeast produces ethanol, not lactate, during anaerobic respiration.

questions.questionText: The first step in scientific research is
questions.explanation: Defining the problem is the first step in scientific research.

questions.questionText: In the modern cell membrane model, called Fluid Mosaic Model,
options: proteins coat the core phospholipid bilayer on both sides
phospholipid bilayer coats the core proteins on both sides
lipid ends and phosphorus-containing ends of the phospholipids form the inner and outer part of the membrane, respectively
lipid ends and phosphorus-containing ends of the phospholipids form the outer and inner part of the membrane, respectively
questions.explanation: In the Fluid Mosaic Model, the phospholipids form a bilayer with their hydrophobic lipid tails pointing inward (forming the core of the membrane) and their hydrophilic phosphorus-containing heads pointing outward, facing both the extracellular environment and the cytoplasm. Proteins are embedded within or attached to this bilayer.

questions.questionText: A senior student studied the effect of enzyme concentration on the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction. The student plotted the reaction rate on the y-axis and the enzyme concentration on the x-axis. The substrate concentration was kept constant. The reaction rate increased linearly from X to Y on the graph, but remained constant from Y to Z as the enzyme concentration increased. Which statement about the graph is correct?
options: Between X and Z, the number of enzyme molecules is limiting
Between Y and Z, the number of enzyme molecules is limiting
Between X and Z, the number of substrate molecules is limiting
Between Y and Z, the number of substrate molecules is limiting
questions.explanation: At point Y, the substrate concentration becomes limiting, causing the reaction rate to plateau.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is/are present in the phloem sap?
questions.explanation: Phloem sap contains sucrose, hormones, and amino acids.

questions.questionText: Lampreys belong to the group:
questions.explanation: Lampreys are classified under Agnatha, which are jawless fish.

questions.questionText: On the basis of their origin, natural resources are categorized as:
questions.explanation: Natural resources are commonly categorized into renewable and non-renewable.

questions.questionText: Drug of choice in giardiasis and Trichomoniasis vaginalis is
questions.explanation: Metronidazole is the drug of choice for both giardiasis and Trichomoniasis vaginalis infections due to its effectiveness against these anaerobic protozoan parasites. It works by disrupting the DNA of these organisms.

questions.questionText: Carbohydrates containing more than two, but less than ten, sugar units are usually known as______________.
questions.explanation: Oligosaccharides are carbohydrates with a small number of sugar units.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct statement regarding Mendel's law of dominance;
options: Every character is coded by a pair of factors
Each sex cell receives one of the factor pairs
One factor of the pair completely masks the effect of the other
The inheritance of one factor is independent of the other(s)
questions.explanation: Mendel's law of dominance states that when two contrasting alleles for a trait are present, only the dominant allele will be expressed in the phenotype, completely masking the effect of the recessive allele. The other options refer to different principles: the law of segregation (options 1 and 2) and the law of independent assortment (option 4).

questions.questionText: The word Ecology was first used and describes as 'the scientific study of the interactions between organisms and their environment' by:
questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel is credited with coining the term ecology.

questions.questionText: Which one is utterly found in Gram-Negative bacteria?
questions.explanation: Both flagella and pili can be found in Gram-negative bacteria.

questions.questionText: _______ the mode of arrangement of sepals or petals on floral bud
questions.explanation: Aestivation refers to the arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud.

questions.questionText: The infective form of Entamoeba histolytica is
questions.explanation: The infective form of Entamoeba histolytica is the quadrinucleate (mature) cyst, not the binucleate cyst. The mature cyst contains four nuclei and is resistant to the external environment, allowing it to survive outside the host.

questions.questionText: The improved version of spread plate method is____________________
questions.explanation: The streak plate method is considered an improved version of the spread plate method as it allows for better isolation of individual colonies and is more effective for obtaining pure cultures.

questions.questionText: Insects which pass through complete metamorphosis undergo through
questions.explanation: Complete metamorphosis includes the stages of egg, larva, pupa, and adult.

questions.questionText: Which one contributes to skin color?
questions.explanation: Melanocytes are responsible for producing melanin, the pigment that determines skin color. The amount and type of melanin produced by melanocytes contribute to the variation in skin pigmentation among individuals and populations.

questions.questionText: The infective Stage of the malaria parasite is
questions.explanation: The sporozoite is the infective stage of the malaria parasite.

questions.questionText: The colony can be found only on the surface of the Petri plate in one of the following________
questions.explanation: The streak plate method allows for colonies to grow only on the surface.

questions.questionText: When in the Benedict test reducing sugar (glucose or fructose) and heated copper ion (Cu2+) of copper sulfate (CuSO4) is reduced to a______ of cuprous oxide (Cu+) is formed.
questions.explanation: A red precipitate indicates the presence of reducing sugars in the Benedict test.

questions.questionText: Which one is correctly spelled considering the handwriting of any scientific names?
questions.explanation: Scientific names follow binomial nomenclature where the genus name (Bacillus) is capitalized and the species name (subtilis) is lowercase. Both are italicized when typed or underlined when handwritten. Therefore, 'Bacillus subtilis' is the correct format.

questions.questionText: Antigenic variation is exhibited by
questions.explanation: Trypanosoma exhibits antigenic variation, a mechanism that allows the parasite to periodically change its surface glycoprotein coat to evade the host immune system. This is particularly characteristic of Trypanosoma brucei, the causative agent of African sleeping sickness.

questions.questionText: Plagiarism is defined as
options: using others' research procedure with citation
questions.explanation: Plagiarism involves taking someone else's ideas without proper citation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following organisms is the most important to fix soil Nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Bacteria, particularly nitrogen-fixing bacteria, are crucial for fixing soil nitrogen.

questions.questionText: Considering the potential health benefits of consuming fish, which factors should not be prioritized when making dietary choices?
options: Nutritive value and essential amino acid content
questions.explanation: From a strictly health benefit perspective, omega fatty acid composition should be prioritized, not deprioritized. Environmental sustainability, while important for ecological reasons, would be less directly related to the immediate health benefits of consuming fish compared to nutritional content and disease prevention.

questions.questionText: Respiratory pigment in vertebrates is:
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin is the primary respiratory pigment in vertebrates.

questions.questionText: Which forms of Nitrogen is the most usable and absorbable by the most plants?
questions.explanation: NO3 (nitrate) is the most usable form of nitrogen for plants.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors does not cause deviation from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?
questions.explanation: A large population size actually helps maintain Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium by minimizing the effects of genetic drift. The other factors (migration, mutation, and natural selection) all cause deviations from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium by changing allele frequencies in a population.

questions.questionText: The hormone that promotes milk release from the mammary glands and that stimulates the uterus to contract is
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is responsible for milk release and uterine contractions.

questions.questionText: When testing for the polysaccharide, starch, to add the Potassium Iodide (KI) solution the presence of a __________ color is a positive test for starch.
questions.explanation: A blue-black color indicates the presence of starch when tested with iodine.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a property of enzymes?
options: Not undergoing change themselves in the reactions they catalyze
Not changing the positions of chemical equilibrium
questions.explanation: Enzymes can only catalyze reactions that are energetically favorable.

questions.questionText: The Nitrification process of the Nitrogen cycle includes:
options: Conversion of Nitrogen to Ammonia by microbes
Conversion of Ammonia to Nitrites and Nitrates by bacteria
Conversion of Nitrates to Nitrites by bacteria
Conversion of Nitrates to gaseous Nitrogen by aerobic bacteria
questions.explanation: Nitrification involves the conversion of ammonia to nitrites and then to nitrates.

questions.questionText: Which of the following feature/s is/are distinguish insects from other classes of Arthropods?
options: Their body divided into three regions (head - thorax - abdomen)
They have three pairs of legs
For most of them, the only arthropods with wings
questions.explanation: Insects are distinguished from other arthropods by a combination of features: (1) their body is divided into three distinct regions - head, thorax, and abdomen; (2) they possess exactly three pairs of jointed legs attached to the thorax; and (3) most insects have wings, which is a feature unique to insects among arthropods. Together, these characteristics form the defining traits of the class Insecta.

questions.questionText: Which part of the flower is used for pollinator attraction?
questions.explanation: Petals are often brightly colored to attract pollinators.

questions.questionText: First jawed vertebrates belong to class:
questions.explanation: Placodermi is the class that includes the first jawed vertebrates.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a land natural ecosystem?
questions.explanation: A rain forest is a land natural ecosystem.

questions.questionText: Which of the following cellular respiration phase is correctly matched with the given event?
options: Glycolysis - occurs in the cytoplasm - produces ethanol and lactic acid
Krebs cycle - occurs in the matrix of mitochondria - produces pyruvic acid
Electron transport chain - occurs in cristae - uses oxygen
Transition stage - occurs in cell membrane - produces most of the ATP's
questions.explanation: The electron transport chain occurs in the cristae of mitochondria and uses oxygen.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding allelic relationship in a natural population?
options: Co-dominance relationship produces a heterozygote having the phenotype of both homozygotes
Over dominance relationship agrees with Mendel's ratios
Incomplete dominance relationship produces the phenotype of either parent
questions.explanation: Only co-dominance relationship produces a heterozygote having the phenotype of both homozygotes. Over dominance does not agree with Mendel's ratios, and incomplete dominance produces an intermediate phenotype, not the phenotype of either parent.

questions.questionText: Select incorrect sentences from the following statements
options: To start up aquaculture, types of species and types of aquacultures must be considered
The electricity and distance from the markets are the determinant for investment in aquaculture
Reproduction mode of fishes include both internal and external fertilization
Integration of aquaculture with others agricultural sectors is called polyculture aquaculture
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that 'Integration of aquaculture with others agricultural sectors is called polyculture aquaculture.' This is actually referred to as integrated agriculture-aquaculture (IAA) systems. Polyculture aquaculture refers to raising multiple species of aquatic organisms together in the same system.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct the composition and level of organizational diversity from bottom to top?
options: Kingdom --> Order --> Class --> Phyla --> Families --> Genera --> Species --> Individual
Genera --> Phyla --> Kingdom --> Order --> Families --> Class --> Species --> Individual
Individual --> Species --> Genera --> Families --> Order --> Class --> Phyla --> Kingdom
Kingdom --> Phyla --> Class --> Order --> Families --> Genera --> Species --> Individual
questions.explanation: The correct order of organizational diversity is from Kingdom to Individual.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Chondrostean endoskeletons are partially made of bone
Holostean's endoskeletons are partially made of bone
Coelacanths are most diversified and modern fish groups
No fish exchange gas through their lungs
questions.explanation: Chondrostean endoskeletons are partially made of bone, which is correct. Holosteans have fully ossified skeletons. Coelacanths are actually ancient fishes with limited diversity, not modern or highly diversified. Some fish, like lungfish, do exchange gases through primitive lungs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about ascomycetes?
options: They produce both asexual and sexual reproductive stages
They produce a sac-like structure known as ascus containing ascospores
They don't have a conidial and teleomorphic states
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes do have conidial and teleomorphic states.

questions.questionText: Based on the number of sugar units, ________ are known as monosaccharide, disaccharides, and polysaccharide.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are categorized into monosaccharides, disaccharides, and polysaccharides based on sugar units.

questions.questionText: The effect of different colors of light on the growth of Arabidopsis thaliana (thale cress) seedlings was studied. Three colors of light were tested: blue (450 nm), orange (600 nm), and red (630 nm). Seedling height, shoot length, and biomass were measured in centimeters, centimeters, and grams, respectively. Under blue light, the recorded measurements were 3.5, 2.8, and 2.4. Under orange light, the recorded measurements were 2.3, 2.0, and 2.8. Under red light, the recorded measurements were 7.4, 6.1, and 3.7. What conclusions can be drawn from the data?
options: White light gives the optimal conditions for photosynthesis.
There is a linear relationship between wavelength of light and plant growth.
There is no correlation between total biomass and plant height.
questions.explanation: The data indicates that red light enhances plant growth.

questions.questionText: A giant bacterium, Epulopiscium fishelsoni was discovered in 1985. Which cell structure(s) would enable biologists to classify Epulopiscium as prokaryotic?
options: Circular DNA free in the cytoplasm.
pair of centrioles close to the nuclear pore
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum throughout the cytoplasm.
cellulose cell wall outside the plasma membrane.
questions.explanation: The presence of circular DNA free in the cytoplasm is characteristic of prokaryotic cells.

questions.questionText: The term vertebrata is synonymous to;
questions.explanation: Vertebrata is most closely synonymous with Craniata, as both terms refer to animals with a cranium or skull. Chordata is a broader phylum that includes vertebrates as well as other subphyla. Urochordata refers specifically to tunicates, and fish is just one class of vertebrates.

questions.questionText: To evaluate a proposal, people may likely read ----- of the proposal instead of reading the whole proposal.
questions.explanation: The abstract provides a summary of the proposal.

questions.questionText: Which of following is true about transport mechanisms of substances across the cell membrane?
options: Ions and hydrophobic molecules easily pass by simple diffusion
Solvents and solutes cross cell membrane by osmosis
Bulk transport does not use cells' ATP unlike active transport
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion does involve membrane proteins.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: Virtual population analysis estimates the abundance of population in water
Virtual population analysis enables the scientist to predict the future catches
Harvesting a fish population with compromising its future yields is called sustainable yield
Habitat quality changes affects the population fishes
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is 'Harvesting a fish population with compromising its future yields is called sustainable yield.' This is wrong because sustainable yield involves harvesting WITHOUT compromising future yields - the statement as written contradicts the definition of sustainability.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following represents seed plants only?
questions.explanation: Spermatophyte refers specifically to seed plants.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following term refers to the death rate of individuals in the population?
questions.explanation: Mortality refers to the death rate in a population.

questions.questionText: The top uppermost layer of the leaf that forms a waterproof barrier and protects tissues inside the leaf and limits the loss of water through evaporation is known as?
questions.explanation: The cuticle is a waxy layer that protects the leaf and reduces water loss.

questions.questionText: In the life cycle of the flowering plant which one represented by diploid (2n)?
questions.explanation: The sporophyte is the diploid stage in the life cycle of flowering plants.

questions.questionText: One is not the contents of saliva?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic nodules are not a component of saliva.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the most diversified microorganism?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are the most diverse group of microorganisms.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true?
options: In DNA molecule, the strands are made of H-bonds between complementary bases
DNA is a double stranded molecule
RNA replicates itself in a similar way as DNA
questions.explanation: DNA is indeed a double-stranded molecule.

questions.questionText: Which one is altered concerning microbial growth measurement?
questions.explanation: Dry weight measurement is often altered or less accurate for microbial growth measurement compared to other methods, as it can be affected by extracellular substances and is labor-intensive. Turbidity measurement and spectrophotometry are more reliable and commonly used methods.

questions.questionText: Water moves from the roots through the vascular tissues and out of the leaves is called _____
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts.

questions.questionText: An inability to maintain homeostasis may lead to death or a disease, a condition known as
questions.explanation: Homeostatic imbalance refers to any condition where the body's internal environment deviates from its normal regulated state. When homeostatic mechanisms fail to maintain stability, various diseases can develop. For example, diabetes is a specific manifestation of homeostatic imbalance in glucose regulation, heart failure results from imbalance in cardiac function, and dehydration is an imbalance in water homeostasis. The term 'homeostatic imbalance' encompasses all such failures in maintaining internal equilibrium.

questions.questionText: Gross Anatomy study about:
questions.explanation: Gross anatomy is the study of anatomical structures that can be observed with the naked eye, without the use of a microscope. It focuses on larger structures rather than microscopic ones, and is not limited to 'large or bloated organs' but includes all macroscopic structures.

questions.questionText: The step of food chain in the ecosystem begins from:
questions.explanation: Food chains begin with autotrophs, which produce energy through photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: In genetic maternal effect;
options: Phenotype of the offspring is determined by the genotype of the mother
Phenotype of the mother determines genotypes of the offspring
Inheritance of associated genes is exclusively maternal
Extent of phenotypic expression depends on the genotype of source parents
questions.explanation: In genetic maternal effect, the mother's genotype influences the phenotype of her offspring.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct answer and encircle on it. Insects are:
options: Arthropods with three pairs of legs
questions.explanation: All statements correctly describe insects.

questions.questionText: One is not a criteria to classify organisms?
questions.explanation: Overall habit is not a standard criterion for classifying organisms.

questions.questionText: If the order of bases after transcription reads AAGCUGUUAC, what would be the sequence on the sense strand of the parental transcribed DNA molecule?
questions.explanation: If the mRNA sequence is AAGCUGUUAC, then the template DNA strand would be TTCGACAATG (with T instead of U). The sense strand is complementary to the template strand, so it would be AAGCTGTTAC (matching the mRNA but with T instead of U).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct the composition and level of Genetic diversity from the bottom to top?
questions.explanation: The correct hierarchical order of genetic diversity from bottom (smallest unit) to top (largest) is: Nucleotides --> Genes --> Chromosomes --> Individuals --> Populations. Nucleotides are the basic building blocks of DNA, which form genes, which are organized into chromosomes, which determine the genetic makeup of individuals, which collectively form populations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correctly represents a eukaryotic cell?
options: double membrane surrounds lysosome, mitochondria, nucleus, Golgi apparatus, and cytoplasm
double membrane surrounds Golgi apparatus but a single membrane surrounds lysosome, mitochondria, nucleus, and cytoplasm
double membrane surrounds mitochondria and nucleus but a single membrane surrounds lysosome, Golgi apparatus, and cytoplasm
double membrane surrounds lysosome and cytoplasm but a single membrane surrounds mitochondria, nucleus, and Golgi apparatus
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells have double membranes around mitochondria and the nucleus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following animals is not a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: Sea squirts are not vertebrates; they are tunicates.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a true fungi?
questions.explanation: Slime molds are not classified as true fungi.

questions.questionText: If a child with blood type 'AB' is born from a type 'A' mother and type 'B' father, what would be the possible genotype(s) of the father?
questions.explanation: For a child to have AB blood type, they must receive an A allele from one parent and a B allele from the other. Since the mother is type A, she contributed the A allele. Therefore, the father must have contributed the B allele. The father is type B, so his genotype could be either BB or BO (where O is recessive to both A and B). Since the options only include BO (and not BB), BO is the correct answer.

questions.questionText: Select the factor that does not favor Ethiopia to have diversified ecosystems with diverse flora and fauna.
questions.explanation: The longitudinal position does not significantly influence biodiversity compared to other factors.

questions.questionText: The culture media that is characterized by its ample agar content is_____
questions.explanation: Solid culture media contain a significant amount of agar.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the ecological service of Ecosystem except:
questions.explanation: Medication is not a direct ecological service provided by ecosystems.

questions.questionText: Choose the incorrect one from the following statements
options: Fishery science covers the processes from cultivating of fishes to supplying them on market
Fishery science integrates the behaviors, ecology and population abundance predicting methods
Various ecology adaptations allowed the fishes to have most diversity among others vertebrates
Dorsal and anal fins help fish to walk in water just as of fore and hind legs of other animals
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is 'Dorsal and anal fins help fish to walk in water just as of fore and hind legs of other animals.' This is incorrect because dorsal and anal fins primarily provide stability and control during swimming, not locomotion like legs. Pectoral and pelvic fins are more analogous to limbs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following does not pass through the lungs in its lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) does not have a lung stage in its lifecycle.

questions.questionText: Which one is considered as the main center for control of internal environment?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the primary control center for maintaining homeostasis.

questions.questionText: Small intestine is the normal habitat of
questions.explanation: Giardia lamblia is commonly found in the small intestine.

questions.questionText: Series of interrelated food chains in a given ecosystem is called a ______________.
questions.explanation: A food web consists of interconnected food chains.

questions.questionText: Among the following statements only one is correct, which one is it?
options: In Ethiopia, most fish product is collected from Marine water
The aquaculture in Ethiopia is highly advanced and it is a source of export of the country
Peciforms, Cypriniformes and Siluriformes are most common commercial fishes in Ethiopia
Salmon, Tuna and Cod are common commercial fishes in Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Peciforms, Cypriniformes, and Siluriformes are indeed common in Ethiopian waters.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a useful insect?
questions.explanation: Silk-worms are useful for silk production.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about Zygomycetes?
options: They reproduce by hyphae without septa
They are the known contaminants of cereals and vegetables
They are one members of higher fungi
questions.explanation: Zygomycetes are not classified as higher fungi.

questions.questionText: Among the following which types of resource is matched correctly with its example?
options: Renewable resource = Fossil fuel, Natural gas and Coal
Abiotic resource = Vegetation, Fish population and Birds
Renewable resource = Sunlight, Air and Water
Biotic resource = Soil, Water, Minerals and Air
questions.explanation: Sunlight, air, and water are examples of renewable resources.
